technical-data.invention-title: SYSTEM FOR AND METHOD OF IMPLEMENTING REFRACTION MAPPING
SYSTEME ET PROCEDE DE MISE EN OEUVRE D'UN MAPPAGE DE REFRACTION

nplcit.text: PATENT ABSTRACTS OF JAPAN vol. 1998, no. 13, 30 November 1998 (1998-11-30) & JP 10 208067 A (NAMCO LTD), 7 August 1998 (1998-08-07)
PATENT ABSTRACTS OF JAPAN vol. 1999, no. 04, 30 April 1999 (1999-04-30) & JP 11 003432 A (SEGA ENTERP LTD), 6 January 1999 (1999-01-06)

abstract.p: A system for implementing a refraction mapping is arranged that a refracted texture address is determined, as a normal vector at an intersection point of a boundary surface of at least two different media and a visual line vector is defined to be n, and as a visual line unit vector is defined to be v, a variable k is determined so that the sum (n + kv) of the normal vector n and a value kv of which the visual line unit vector v is multiplied by a variable k becomes parallel to the texture plane. At least two different media are an air, water or a glass. In such system, an object has a portion projecting from the water surface, and a portion sinking under the water, and for at least a portion of the texture associated with the portion sinking under the water, a refracted texture address that is to be displaced according to a refraction phenomena can be determined.

La présente invention concerne un système de mise en oeuvre d'un mappage de réfraction par lequel on détermine une adresse de texture réfractée prenant la forme d'un vecteur normal coupant en un point la surface de séparation entre au moins deux milieux. On définit un vecteur ligne de vision "n" et un vecteur de ligne de vision "v". On calcule ensuite une variable "k" telle que la somme n + kv définisse une parallèle au plan de texture. Deux des milieux considérés sont l'air, l'eau et le verre. Un tel système permet de placer un objet à la surface de séparation, une partie immergée, et une partie émergée. Et pour au moins une partie de la texture associée à la partie immergée, il est possible de calculer une adresse de texture réfractée que l'on doit déplacer en fonction d'un phénomène de réfraction.

description.p: DESCRIPTION
SYSTEM FOR AND METHOD OF IMPLEMENTING REFRACTION MAPPING
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a refraction mapping technique for producing an image as if looking an object through a refraction phenomena, for example, in an information equipment which includes an entertainment system such as a video game device and the like.
Description of the Related Art

For example, in the video game device, when looking at the bottom of the sea through the water surface, it looks like the bottom of the sea to be distorted due to the refraction phenomena. A refraction mapping is known as a method of producing a realistic picture by simulating the phenomena as described above.

It is required in a conventional refraction mapping for a land portion protruding from the water surface and a portion sinking under the water sinking to implement separately a parallel projection rendering, in a vertical direction onto the water surface, thereby making the burdens for a central processing unit (CPU), a graphic processing unit (GPU) and the likes to be large.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

Accordingly, in the light of the above-mentioned problems, it is an object of the present invention to provide a system for and a method of implementing a refraction mapping with an easy method, as well as a recording medium for the method.

A system for implementing a refraction mapping according to the present
invention, includes means for perspective-projecting an object, and for producing a two-dimensional texture of the object for a texture plane; and means for determining a refracted texture address that displaces according to a refraction phenomena, for at least a portion of the texture, wherein the refracted texture address is determined, depending on a normal vector at a boundary surface of different media and a visual line vector.

It is preferable that, in the above-described system for implementing the refraction mapping according to the present invention, the refracted texture address is determined by an angle formed with the normal vector and the visual line vector or a component of the normal vector that is parallel to the texture plane.

Preferably, in the above-described system for implementing the refraction mapping according to the present invention, as a normal vector at an intersection point of the boundary surface of at least two different media and the visual line vector is defined to be n, and as the visual line unit vector is defined to be v, determining a variable k so that the sum (n + kv) of the normal vector n and the value kv of which the visual line unit vector v is multiplied by a variable k becomes parallel to the texture plane, and the texture address is displaced by an amount of a constant multiplication of (n + kv), that is L (n + kv).
Further, the texture address may be displaced with only an amount of L (nχ, ny) of which two components (nχ, ny) parallel to the texture plane of the normal vector n are multiplied by a constant L.
At this moment, at least two different media may represent the ones with different refractive indices such as an air, water or a glass.

It is preferable that, the above-described system for implementing the refraction mapping according to the present invention, further includes means for displacing at least a portion of a texture, based on the refracted texture address; and means for perspective-transforming on a screen, using this displaced texture.
In such system, the object has a portion projecting from the water surface, and a portion sinking under the water, and for at least a portion of the texture associated with the portion sinking under the water, a refracted texture address that is to be displaced according to a refraction phenomena can be determined. Further, such system is preferably provided in a video game device.

In the above-described system for implementing the refraction mapping, the texture plane is defined on a plane perpendicular to the Z-axis that is in a visual line direction of a view point coordinate system, and for example, it makes possible to rendering the part (the water bottom part) under the water surface with the same procedure as the perspective projection of the land part protruding from the water surface of the topography, and as a result, a creation of a texture for use in a refraction can be made by implementing collectively the land part and the water bottom part with just one rendering.

According to this system for implementing the rendering, an amount of a displacement generated by a refraction phenomena will not satisfy the Snell's law exactly, regarding the picture of the water bottom part under the water. However, as obtaining an amount of a displacement that is an approximate to the Snell's law using an easy method, it makes possible to qualitatively rendering the water bottom part under the water. Further, a method of implementing a refraction mapping according to the present invention includes the steps of: perspective-projecting an object, and producing a two-dimensional texture of the object for a texture plane; and determining a refracted texture address that displaces according to a refraction phenomena, for at least a portion of the texture, wherein the refracted texture address is determined, depending on a normal vector at a boundary surface of different media and a visual line vector.

Preferably, in the method of implementing the refraction mapping according to
the present invention, the refracted texture address is determined by an angle formed with the normal vector and the visual line vector or a component of the normal vector that is parallel to the texture plane.

In the method of implementing the refraction mapping according to the present invention, as a normal vector at an intersection point of the boundary surface of at least two different media and the visual line vector is defined to be n, and as the visual line unit vector is defined to be v, determining a variable k so that the sum (n + kv) of the normal vector n and the value kv of which the visual line unit vector v is multiplied by a variable k becomes parallel to the texture plane, the refracted texture address is displaced by an amount of a constant multiplication of (n + kv), that is L (n + kv).

Moreover, the refracted texture address may be displaced with only an amount of L (nχ, ny) of which two components (nx, ny) parallel to the texture plane of the normal vector n are multiplied by a constant L.

The controller 20 connected to the controller connection unit 9 has 16 instruction keys, for example, for inputting an instruction from a user, and transmits a state of this instruction key to the communication controller 91 about 60 times/second, with a synchronous communication, in accordance with the instruction from the communication controller 91. As a result, an instruction from a user is inputted into the CPU 51, and the CPU 51 performs a process in accordance with an instruction from a user, based on the game program and the likes that are being executed.

Herein, among the main memory 53, the GPU 62, the image decoder 64 and the decoder 82 and the likes, it is necessary to transfer a large quantity of the image data in a high speed at a time when implementing a reading of a program, a display of an image or a drawing and the likes. Thus, in this video game device, it is configured as enabling to implement a so-called DMA transfer that implement directly a transfer of the data among the main memory 53, the GPU 62, the image decoder 64 and the decoder 82 and the likes according to a control from the peripheral device control unit 52 without going through the CPU 51 as described above. As a result, it enables to reduce a load of the CPU 51, and to implement a high speed data transfer.

Further, if it is necessary to store the setting data and the likes of the game that is being executed, the CPU 51 transmits the data that is to be stored to the communication controller 91, and the communication controller 91 writes the data from the CPU 51 into the memory card 10 or the portable electronics equipment 100 that is inserted into a slot of the memory card insertion unit 8A or of the memory card insertion unit 8B.

The memory card 10 and/or the portable electronics equipment 100 are separated from the bus BUS, and they can be attached/detached in a state that the main body of the device is being energized. Accordingly, when the storage capacities of the memory card 10 and/or the portable electronics equipment 100 run short, and the likes, it enables to insert a new memory card, without shutting down the power supply of the main body of the device. As a result, without losing the game data necessary to be backed up, by inserting a new memory card, the necessary data can be written into the new memory card.

In the entertainment system as described above, the refraction mapping according to the present embodiment is implemented.
[Refraction Mapping]

Then, in the entertainment system according to the present embodiment, the embodiments of the system for and method of implementing the refraction mapping will be described in detail with reference to the accompanying drawings.

Various kinds of techniques are known regarding to the mapping. When a man is looking at the water bottom WB through the water surface, as standing by a waterside of a pond or a swimming pool, an object at the water bottom WB looks as being distorted by refraction. A method of producing a realistic picture of the object being at the water bottom WB, by simulating the phenomena such as described above, is called as a refraction mapping.

A similar refraction phenomenon is also occurred when observing an object through a transparent glass and the likes, other than the water surface. That is, when looking at an object, through two or more kinds of transparency or semi-transparency media, the object looks as being displaced by an effect of a refraction phenomena of a light that is generated at a boundary surface of these media. Accordingly, when producing such a picture of the object, the refraction mapping technique is utilized.

The refraction mapping is a CG (Computer Graphics) technique for mapping, by calculating how an object looks, when a refraction phenomena intervenes on a line of sight between a view point NP and the object.
(The refraction mapping that is presently implemented)

In order to make the refraction mapping according to the present embodiment
more easily understandable, at first, the procedure of the refraction mapping that is presently implemented will be simply described.

In the CG image, projecting an object shape onto a two-dimensional screen (a rendering), and mapping a texture for the object shape obtained (a texture mapping). In Fig. 5 there are shown the water surface WL and the water bottom WB.

Water of a depth DPT is filled in just a gap between the water surface and the water bottom WB. There is an air above the water. Herein, it is assumed that a refractive index of an air is nl, and a refractive index of water is n2.

It is further assumed that the view point NP is at the upper left, and there is a screen SC in front thereof. The view point NP means that there is a human eye at this location, and looking at the water bottom (object) therefrom. Fig. 5 shows a state in which there is a line of sight NL toward a point A on the water of the surface from the view point NP, and looking at this point A. In the figure, there are shown a case in which the line of sight NL travels straight when there is no water, and a case in which the line of sight NL is refracted, as there is water. Further, in the description herein, it is assumed that the water bottom WB is a flat.

In Fig. 5, when there is no water, the line of sight NL toward the point A from the view point NP travels straight as it is, and then reaches to a point D at the water bottom WB. That is, looking at the point D. Accordingly, when drawing the water bottom WB on the screen SC, perspective-transforming the point D that constitutes a 3-dimensional object so as to display it as a 2-demensional figure on the screen SC, rendering, and then texture mapping. That is, when texture mapping, drawing a texture of the point D at where the line of sight is across the water bottom WB, at the P on the screen SC. In the following, when the water is stored only with the water depth DPT from the water bottom WB, the line of sight NL toward the point A from the view point NP reaches to a point C at the water bottom, as a refraction is occurred at a point A of the
boundary surface of an air and the water surface. When looking at the point A on the water surface from the view point NP, the point C at the water bottom is to be seen. Accordingly, the texture of the point C has to be mapped on the point P on the screen SC. In other words, a light emitted from the point C that exists at the water bottom

(the point C that constitutes the object that exists at the water bottom) is entered into the view point VP as following the visual line NL, as being refracted at the point A on the water surface WL. Because the man's eye can not sensuously understand this refraction, it is under an illusion as the visual line NL toward the point A from the view point NP travels straight as it is, and it looks as if the point C at the water bottom WB exists at the point D.

Now, it is to quantitatively calculate a location of the point C that can be seen when looking at the point A on the water surface from the view point VP. The location of the point C is calculated from the Snell's Law as follows. Herein, at the point A, a normal n is defined as being perpendicularly from the water surface WL. Assuming an angle formed by the visual line VL and the normal n to be . Assuming an angle formed by the refracted visual line VL-1 and the normal n to be β. Further, assuming a depth of the water to be DPT. At this moment, the following equations hold according to the Snell's law. nl- sinα = n2- sinβ (1)

Herein, as considering a triangle ADB and a triangle ACB, the following relations hold. sin = BD/AD (2) tanβ =BC/AB = BC/DPT (3) From these relations, transforming the equation (1), and substituting the equation (2), then it forms the following equation. sinβ = (nl/n2)- sinα = (nl/n2 (BD/AD) (4)
Further, between sin and cos, there is the following relation.
(sinβ)2 + (cosβ)2 = 1 (5)
Transforming the equation (3), and substituting the equations (4) and (5), then it becomes as follows. BC = DPT tanβ = DPT- (sinβ/cosβ)
= DPT sinβ- {1 - (sinβ)2}1 2

Looking at the equation (6), DPT is a depth of the water, nl and n2 are the refractive indices of the air and the water, respectively, BD and AD are the values that are determined by the visual line VL, and thus enabling to calculate the value of BC.
Accordingly, with the equation (6), the location of the point C that constitutes the object at the water bottom at a time when the water exists can be determined.

As a result, at the point P on the screen SC on which the point D is drawn when there is no water, the point C is drawn in place of the point D when there is water. Accordingly, it makes possible of rendering the water bottom WB.

It is assumed in the above description that the water bottom WB is to be flat. However, in general, an actual topography is not a simple plane, but there is usually an unevenness on the surface thereof. It is necessary to draw such the water bottom WB in a three-dimensional graphics. When rendering the topography constituted of such unevenness, the topography texture is not a sheet of texture, but it becomes a polyhedron configured in three-dimensionally.
For such case, in Fig. 6, a topographic texture located parallel to the water surface WL is defined beneath the water bottom WB.

Next, for the topography in a case of assuming that no water exists, in advance, a two-dimensional texture is produced on this texture plane. Concretely, performing a three-dimension calculation for the topography having an unevenness, implementing a shading, pasting it on a texture plane by parallel-projecting from a direction which is
perpendicular to the water surface WL, so as to produce a two-dimensional (flat) texture of this topography.

Then, the refraction mapping is implemented by using this two-dimensional topographic texture. In this moment, this topography may be continued with the land that is higher than the water surface WL. For the land protruding from the water surface WL, no refraction is occurred, so that a rendering has to be made by executing a calculation of a perspective transformation that uses a rotation and a coordinate transformation, from a direction of the view point VP. On the other hand, for the topography under the water (the water bottom WB), because a displacement by a refraction phenomenon is occurred, the refracted texture address is obtained by calculating an amount of its displacement using the equation (6) in regard with each of the points that constitute the water bottom WB.
As described above, the method that is presently implemented is owing to such complex procedures. Fig. 7 is a drawing showing one example of an actual refraction mapping.
At first, in the first step, implementing a parallel-projection or a parallel paste to the entire topography, for a texture plane which is parallel to the water surface WL.

Fig. 7 A shows a state in which a rendering is made for the water bottom WB having no water with the parallel-projection. This rendering is executed in the GPU 62, and it is drawn on a texture area other than a display area of the frame buffer 63, with the data obtained.

In the second step, because it seems to be refracted when looking at the topographic part under the water in the air, a rendering is made as obtaining the refracted texture address, using the Snell's law described above. Fig. 7 B shows a state in which an image of the water surface (an image of the water bottom WB that is seen through the water) is produced in a display area of the frame buffer 63, by
implementing the refraction mapping, taking the memory image of Fig. 7 A as the texture.

In the third step, because no refraction phenomenon is occurred in the topographic part protruding from the water surface WL, a rendering is made to this topographic part by obtaining a texture address using a perspective transformation technique. Fig. 7 C shows a state in which the one on which the water is rendering the land part with the perspective projection is drawn on an image of the water surface that is produced in the display area illustrated in Fig. 7 B and thus it is superimposed.

Accordingly, after the parallel projection, it is required to implement the renderings in two directions with the perspective projection. Because this drawing method at the present time implements the renderings in two directions, and superimposes them, the work becomes more complex, and the loads of the CPU and the GPU become much heavier, and the drawing time becomes also longer. (The Refraction Mapping According to The Present Embodiment) In the following, it is described about a method of implementing refraction mapping according to the present embodiment. This method of implementing the refraction mapping may be programmed, and thus may be provided in a state of being recorded solely into a recording medium such as an optical disk, or may be provided along with a game software as a part of the game software. This program for implementing the refraction mapping is activated on the entertainment system, and is executed with the CPU 51 thereof.

The meaning of that the program for implementing the refraction mapping is provided as being solely recorded in the recording medium is to be prepared for the software engineers in advance as a library, for use in an application program development such as a game software and the likes. As is well known, it is required an enormous time to produce all functions of the software anew, at a time of developing software.
However, in general, when decomposing the functions that constitute a software into the classes of the functions, it is appreciated that there includes the functions commonly used for the various kinds of software such as a parallel movement of an object, for example. Thus, it becomes significant to provide the function of implementing the refraction mapping according to the present embodiment, as a library program, for a software engineer, in advance. As receiving a supply as a program from an outside in advance, for these common functions, the software engineer enables to concentrate on producing only an essential part peculiar to that program other than the common functions.

Fig. 8 shows a case in which an angle l formed by the visual line VL and the normal n is relatively smaller, comparing to Fig. 5. In such case, refraction at the surface the water WL becomes smaller comparing to the one in Fig. 5. In the present embodiment, as paying attention to a character such that if the angle α formed by the visual line VL and the normal n is large, an amount of a refraction occurred at the boundary of the air and the water is also large, and on the contrary, if the angle α formed by the visual line VL and the normal n is small, the amount of the refraction is also small, it is intended to implement the refraction mapping with a simple calculation method by qualitatively imitating the above character. This rendering method is, strictly speaking, not matched with the Snell's law, regarding the picture of the water bottom part under the water. That is, at a time of the rendering, an amount of a displacement generated by refraction phenomena will not satisfy the Snell's law exactly. However, as obtaining an amount of a displacement that is an approximate to the Snell's law using an easy method to be described below, qualitatively rendering the water bottom part under the water becomes possible.

In Fig. 9, a view point coordinate system is set to be a Y-Z plane as shown on
the paper of the drawing, and the X-axis is set in a direction perpendicular to the paper.

The present embodiment is, as shown in Fig. 9, a method that defines a texture plane on a plane perpendicular to the Z-axis, and makes it possible to rendering the part (the water bottom part) under the water surface WL with the same procedure as the perspective projection of the land part protruding from the water surface WL of the topography, and as a result, implementing collectively the land part and the water bottom part with just one rendering.

As shown in Fig. 9, in advance, the one on which an entire topography is drawn by perspective-transforming in the visual line direction is set to be a topographic texture. The topographic texture is placed perpendicular to the Z-axis of the viewpoint coordinate system. Further, the topographic texture plane and the screen surface SC are in a parallel positional relation.

At first, in a state that there is no water, the topography is perspective-projected on the texture plane. A three-dimensional topography is perspective-projected for the texture plane from the view point VP. Concretely, the texture address of the point a that constitutes the topography is set to be the point A on the topographic texture plane, the texture address of the point b that constitutes the topography is set to be the point B on the topographic texture plane, and the texture address of the point c that constitutes the topography is set to be the point C on the topographic texture plane.

In the next step, for this topography, it is considered a state in which there is water, and a portion of the topography shown in Fig. 9 is under the water. As shown in Fig. 10, it is a case in which there is water up to the water surface WL, and a portion of the topography remains as a land. In such case, the topography under the water (the part of the water bottom) looks as if being displaced, according to the refraction phenomena occurred at the boundary of the air and the water. In the present embodiment, an amount of this displacement is calculated using an easy calculation
method.

In the model as show in Fig. 10, at an intersection point of the visual line vector and the water surface WL, a normal vector for the water surface WL is set to be n, and the one in which the visual line vector is normalized is set to be a visual line unit vector v. A variable k is determined so that the sum (n + kv) of the normal vector n and the value kv of which the visual line unit vector v is multiplied by a variable k becomes perpendicular to the Z-axis.

As illustrating by using Fig. 10, the variable k is determined so that the vector (n + kv) is parallel to the texture plane. Since the texture plane is placed perpendicular to the Z-axis, if the vector (n + kv) is parallel to the texture plane (i.e., it is on the texture plane), the Z coordinate of the vector (n + kv) becomes zero. Accordingly, the following equation (7) holds. nz + kvz = 0 (7)

Herein, nz represents Z value (scalar quantity) of the normal vector n, and kvz represents Z value (scalar quantity) of the vector kv. Transforming the equation (7), the following equation (8) is obtained. k = - nz / vz (8)

Looking at the equation (8), nz is Z value of the normal vector, and vz is Z value of the visual line unit vector, and both are known values. Accordingly, the k can be determined from the equation (8).

The visual line VL from the air into the water is, as described in relation to Fig. 5, refracted in a clockwise direction at the boundary surface thereof. Accordingly, obtaining (n + kv) using such k, and by adding a negative (-) symbol thereto, - (n + kv) is set to be a displacement address of a texture. Herein, in general, L (n + kv) is used, in which a constant L is multiplied according to the sizes of two kinds of the refractive indices. Further, as a more easy method, among three components (nχ, ny, nz) of the normal vector n, L (nχ, ny) in
which two components (nχ, ny) parallel to the texture plane are multiplied by a constant L, may be used as the displacement address.

Mapping the water bottom WB using the displacement address obtained as described above, the rendering is made to the refracted part of the water bottom. Since the land part was finished of the rendering at a time when the perspective projection to the texture plane was performed, by superimposing with this image, the rendering can be made to both parts of the water bottom and the land.

As described above, this rendering method is such that an amount of a displacement occurred by a refraction phenomena will not satisfy the Snell's law precisely, regarding to the picture of the water bottom under the water. However, by obtaining an amount of a displacement that is an approximate to the Snell's law using an easy method, the rendering can be made qualitatively to the part of the water bottom under the water.

In the above-described refraction mapping that is implemented at the present time, it is necessary to perform two directional renderings for a parallel projection and a perspective projection. However, the refraction mapping described in the present embodiment can be implemented by only one directional rendering, by performing the refraction mapping using the water bottom texture produced by the perspective projection and the texture displacement quantity that can be calculated from the normal of the water surface WL and the visual line vector.

Further, as shown in Fig. 10, it is not necessarily true that the water surface WL always forms a flat plane. The water surface such as an ocean surface is, usually in a state of which waves are formed. Fig. 11 shows the water surface WL of which such waves are formed. In this case, when the waves are formed on the water surface WL, the angle α formed by the normal n and the visual line VL becomes smaller as the normal n approaching to be parallel to the visual line VL, and as a consequence, an amount of a
displacement of the displacement address - (n + kv) becomes smaller, and on the contrary, the angle oc formed by the normal n and the visual line VL becomes larger as the normal n approaching to be a right-angle with respect to the visual line VL, and as a consequence, an amount of a displacement of the displacement address - (n + kv) becomes larger. As a result of this, the one that is an approximate to the displacement according to the refraction phenomena occurred at the boundary of the air and the water can be obtained.

Fig. 11 is a diagram illustrating this relation. The normal vector is such that a direction thereof varies according to a state of a wave. Herein, there are exemplified the normal vector nl that is approximately perpendicular to the visual line VL, and the normal vector n2 that is approximately in parallel therewith. For the normal vector nl, kl is determined so that the vector (nl + klv) is parallel to the texture plane.

Similarly, for the normal vector n2, k2 is determined so that the vector (n2 + k2v) is parallel to the texture plane. As described above, by setting the amount of displacement to be - (nl + klv), - (n2 + k2v), depending on the states of waves, it enables to make the amount of displacement to be relatively large in the normal vector nl that is approximately perpendicular to the visual line VL, and to be relatively small in the normal vector n2 that is approximately parallel to the visual line VL.

The state of the normal vector nl that is approximately perpendicular to the visual line VL is a case in which the amount of displacement is relatively large because the angle α is relatively large as shown in Fig. 5, and on the other hand, the state of the normal vector n2 that is approximately parallel to the visual line VL is a case in which the amount of displacement is relatively small because the angle α is relatively small as shown in Fig. 8. As a result, at the water surface WL on which the waves are formed, it also makes possible to implement the refraction mapping that follows the Snell's law qualitatively.

Fig. 12 is a diagram showing one example of the refraction mapping according
to the present embodiment. Fig. 12 A shows that, in a state of being no water, the one on which a rendering is made to a topography with a perspective projection is drawn to a display area at where it is outputted as a video output of the frame buffer 63. Fig. 12 B shows a state in which, with an image of the display area produced in Fig. 12 A as a texture, for the water bottom WB under the water surface WL, an image of the water surface (an image of the water bottom WB under the water surface WL) that is produced by implementing the refraction mapping, as an amount of displacement being obtained by a refraction with the above-described easy method, is superimposed with an image of the display area that is drawn in Fig. 12 A. Consequently, at a time when implementing the refraction mapping, without preparing an orthogonal projection of an image that is displayed as being refracted, by modifying the image that is perspective-projected on the screen SC, it can be represented with a simple method.

According to the present invention, it makes possible to provide a system for and a method of implementing refraction mapping with an easy method, as well as a recording media in which this method is recorded.

The invention may be embodied in other specific forms without departing from the spirit or essential characteristics thereof. The present embodiments are therefore to be considered in all respects as illustrative and not restrictive, the scope of the invention being indicated by the appended claims rather than by foregoing description and all changes which come within the meaning and range of equivalency of the claims are therefore intended to be embraced therein.

2. The system for implementing a refraction mapping according to claim 1, wherein said refracted texture address is determined by an angle formed with said normal vector and said visual line vector or a component of said normal vector that is parallel to said texture plane.
